raw_case_text: We report a 39-year-old caucasian man who has lived in Angola for 4 years. He presented to a hospital in California, during a trip, with a flu-like syndrome, jaundice and altered state of consciousness. On hospital admission, he had hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, acidemia and acute renal failure. After the diagnosis of Plasmodium falciparum malaria, the patient initiated therapy with quinine and doxycycline, although developing severe encephalopathy (coma). After therapy with artesunate, he had hematologic and neurological improvement, and was transferred to Portugal. On initial eye examination at our hospital, he had 20/20 visual acuity in the right eye and a central scotoma in the left eye. Right eye indirect ophthalmoscopy revealed round deep layer retinal hemorrhage, with one disc diameter of radius, in the superior temporal arcade (Figure 1 (Fig. 1)). Left eye indirect ophthalmoscopy showed a foveal hemorrhage, several superficial hemorrhages in the interpapillomacular bundle (Figure 2 (Fig. 2)) and a deep white-centered peripheral hemorrhagic lesion (Figure 3 (Fig. 3)). Fluorescein angiography was not performed given the deterioration of the renal function warranting hemodialysis. At one-month follow-up, the patient had 20/20 visual acuity in both eyes and on examination almost all lesions shown on retinography had regressed (Figure 4 (Fig. 4) and Figure 5 (Fig. 5)).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 39-year-old male presenting with a flu-like illness, jaundice, acute visual scotoma, and rapid progression to altered consciousness while traveling.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, who had lived in Angola for 4 years, developed a progressive flu-like syndrome, jaundice, and deteriorating sensorium while traveling in California. Upon hospital admission, he was found to have acute hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, metabolic acidemia, and acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis. Despite initial oral therapy, his encephalopathy progressed to deep coma, prompting conversion to intravenous artesunate. Following neurological recovery, he noted acute central vision loss in the left eye and was repatriated to Portugal for specialized ophthalmologic and nephrologic management.
subjective.past_medical_history: Lived in Angola for 4 years prior to presentation. No prior ocular or nephrologic history documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, malaise, jaundice, altered sensorium, and left eye central visual scotoma. Negative for prior visual impairment. Medications: quinine, doxycycline, and artesunate received during hospitalization. Allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Initially comatose with deep encephalopathy and jaundice; later fully conscious and oriented. Visual acuity: Right eye 20/20, left eye with central scotoma (subsequently improving to 20/20 at 1 month). Dilated fundoscopic examination: Right eye revealed round deep intraretinal hemorrhage (one disc diameter in radius) along the superior temporal vascular arcade; left eye revealed prominent foveal hemorrhage, multiple superficial flame-shaped hemorrhages within the papillomacular bundle, and a deep white-centered peripheral hemorrhagic lesion (Roth spot). Systemic examination: Hemodialysis catheter in situ; lungs clear, abdomen soft.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission laboratory investigations demonstrated acute hemolytic anemia, marked thrombocytopenia, systemic acidemia, and severe acute renal failure with azotemia necessitating hemodialysis.
objective.advanced_workup: Color retinal photography / indirect ophthalmoscopy: Documented multifocal malarial retinopathy including foveal hemorrhage, papillomacular hemorrhages, and white-centered intraretinal hemorrhages (fluorescein angiography contraindicated and deferred due to renal dysfunction).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe cerebral Plasmodium falciparum malaria complicated by malarial coma, acute hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, severe metabolic acidemia, acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis, and acute malarial retinopathy with foveal hemorrhage and left central scotoma.
Diagnostic confirmation: Detection and laboratory confirmation of Plasmodium falciparum malaria on admission blood films.
Plan & Outcome: Initial treatment with oral quinine and doxycycline was escalated to parenteral artesunate upon development of deep coma, resulting in successful parasite clearance and neurological revival. Acute renal failure was managed with temporary hemodialysis. Left central scotoma and retinal hemorrhages were managed conservatively; by 1-month follow-up, visual acuity normalized to 20/20 bilaterally with near-total regression of all fundoscopic hemorrhages and complete renal recovery.
